key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on the connections of physical neural networks can greatly improve efficiency for smooth, continuous control tasks by turning each link into a learnable computational element.
engineering_relevance: The approach suggests a path to ultra-low-power analogue hardware—projected around 30 microwatts—for robotic control, kinematics, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking.
method: Train nonlinear connection functions inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold networks instead of using only scalar weights.
Implement the functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Validate transfer to hardware across ~35,000 connections and compare with memristive simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that these networks achieve far fewer nodes and connections than multilayer perceptrons on smooth regression/control tasks, but not on classification-like decision boundaries.
watch_item: The benefit is task-dependent, so the architecture may not provide parameter-efficiency gains for sharply non-smooth or classification-style problems.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
